claim.quote: Here we report high-precision cyclotron frequency comparisons of a single antiproton and a negatively charged hydrogen ion (H−) carried out in a Penning trap system.

key_value_text.quote: Our precision of 69 parts per trillion exceeds the energy resolution of previous antiproton-to-proton mass comparisons
key_value_text.value: Charge-to-mass ratio comparison at a precision of 69 parts per trillion

name: High-precision comparison of the antiproton-to-proton charge-to-mass ratio

significance.quote: so our result shows that the CPT theorem holds at the atto-electronvolt scale
significance.value: Precision of 69 parts per trillion; result consistent with the CPT theorem at the atto-electronvolt scale

summary.plain: BASE compared the way a single antiproton and a negatively charged hydrogen ion circle in a magnetic field, 13,000 times. The ratios of charge to mass agree to 69 parts per trillion, a test of the CPT symmetry.
summary.technical: Cyclotron-frequency comparison of a single antiproton and an H− ion in a Penning trap at 29.6 MHz, 13,000 measurements; antiproton-to-proton charge-to-mass ratio compared at a precision of 69 parts per trillion, consistent with CPT invariance at the atto-electronvolt scale.

title: High-precision comparison of the antiproton-to-proton charge-to-mass ratio
why_it_matters: The abstract says the precision exceeds the energy resolution of previous antiproton-to-proton mass comparisons by a factor of four.
